Verified against the code on 3 Oct 2026, then re-checked line by line against the critique. The coverage doc is stale in two places: DOB is now captured on the admit form, and the made-up appointment rows are gone.

REGISTRATION / IDENTITY
- No registration path exists. Every patients row comes from an inpatient admission: admission_service.admit_patient (server/services/admission_service.py:223-480).
  - It always mints PAT-xxxx and a random MRN-XXXXXX when the MRN is blank (:248-249), always creates a Bridge portal login (:263), always inserts an 'active' admission, a patient_profiles row (:335), a new case_room channel (:432-436) and a sage_room_memory row (:470-480).
  - The route is doctor-only (patient.write, server/routes/admission_routes.py:79-113).
  - Typing an MRN that already exists hits patients.mrn UNIQUE (server/database.py:50) and comes back as a 500 "Admission failed". A returning patient can never be readmitted onto their own record.
- Legacy POST /api/vigil/patients (vigil_routes.py:974-1048) still creates a status-'admitted' ghost with no admissions row. Callers: the dead wrapper createPatient (src/api/client.ts:2119), server/scripts/soak_test.py:249, server/tests/test_patient_name_rule.py:108-122.
- patients.status CHECK allows only admitted/discharged/transferred (database.py:55). About 35 schema definitions reference patients(id), so a new status is an FK-parent rebuild (the users-rebuild trap, migrations.py:4697-4815). sage_relay_context.py:217 reads COALESCE(p.status,'admitted').
- DOB is captured on the admit form (src/components/AdmitPatientModal.tsx:102,179) and stored only when usable (admission_service.py:16-41; discharge_access_service.usable_dob:100). DOB is the discharge-link second factor.
- No demographic edit path. The only UPDATE patients writers are discharge (discharge_service.py:648), transfer (frontdesk_service.py:1202) and the two importers.
- Lookup: /api/search/patients returns ADMITTED patients only, dept-scoped and audited (search_routes.py:26-127). No phone, DOB or ABHA search.
- Duplicates: only the history importer reports them (history_import_service.py:83,159).
- ABHA: abha_identities/abha_verifications exist (migrations.py:3294-3370); abdm_service.record_abha (:744) always records 'unverified', opens its own session, reachable only from the ABDM desk.
- Numbering: document_number_series/next_document_number (migrations.py:2100-2113, billing_masters.py:651-708) reset yearly and embed the year; an unconfigured series issues placeholders.

ALLERGIES
- patient_allergies is what the interlocks screen. admit_patient charts allergy chips through clinical_records_service.record_allergies_on(db, ...) (admission_service.py:352-361; migration 40 backfilled the gap).
- There is NO way to record 'asked, no known allergies'. clinical_records_service.allergy_entries drops 'nkda'/'none' (:34-44), and allergy_interlock.py:360-366 states Orb cannot tell NKDA from never asked; it reports allergies_on_file only.

SCOPE
- permissions.patient_in_scope (permissions.py:447-468) fail-closes any patient with no admission. PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL (:428-432) resolves a discharged patient to their LAST admission's department.
- require_patient_access (permissions.py:663-720) is ONE guard for reads AND writes. Writes behind it with no admitted-status check include add_patient_medication (vigil_routes.py:907-950, medication.write, which nurses hold) and nurse obs (nurse_routes.py:177, vitals.write; record_observation scores NEWS2 and posts to Relay). Widening patient_in_scope would open them.
- Sage keeps a deliberate duplicate (sage_service._patient_in_scope, sage_service.py:1933-1960), pinned equal by test_the_route_scope_and_the_sage_scope_agree (test_patient_scope_routes.py:520-540). sage_routes.py:3412-3422 uses permissions.enforce_patient_scope and scope_patient_ids_sql for provenance. An out-of-scope view_context patient is silently not anchored and Sage may fall back to the thread's patient (sage_service.py:3727-3740).
- The GET drift guard (test_patient_scope_routes.py:580-630) has an empty exempt set; test_nurse_write_scope.py covers the nurse POSTs.

OPD (front desk)
- opd_visits and patient_movements are created lazily by frontdesk_service.ensure_frontdesk_schema (:152-286), not by a numbered migration. opd_visits.status allows waiting/in_consultation/completed/cancelled only.
- Token engine per (date, department, doctor) under an immediate transaction plus a partial unique index. Consulting doctor must be an active clinician of that clinic (F151).
- opd_registration_allowed (:531-556): a pure outpatient (no admission ever) is registrable by ANY department; a patient with any past admission falls through to patient_in_scope, so a patient discharged from Cardiology cannot be registered into Ortho OPD by a departmented desk. A doctor holds patient.write and passes require_frontdesk_write, so a doctor can register a visit in their own clinic for any pure outpatient.
- create_opd_visit refuses a department other than the caller's (frontdesk_routes.py:296-370). Register/start/complete/cancel audits are written after commit in fail-soft 'clinical_record'.
- require_frontdesk_write and require_frontdesk_read both depend on require_permission(PATIENT_READ_ALL) (frontdesk_routes.py:164-207), so no account without chart access can use the desk. FRONTDESK_WRITE is held by admin only; roles.py has no front-office role. admin holds no patient.write (permissions.py:288-334).
- The queue route writes a phi_access row on every non-empty read (frontdesk_routes.py:262-275).
- Completion raises one OPD-CONSULT line as 'op', unpriced rather than Rs 0 (frontdesk_service.py:576-688). billing_service.cancel_charge exists (:752).
- UI: FrontDeskPanel picks patients from /vigil/patients?limit=200 (admitted only); the tab is admin-only (shellConfig.tsx:711-712). Missing: doctor queue, call/skip/priority, token board, consultation note, OPD prescription.
- Socket: connect() joins dept rooms only for vitals.read holders (ws/realtime.py:270-287). realtime.schedule_on_loop (:419) is the importable sync-to-loop emit helper.

APPOINTMENTS
- No doctor and no slot (database.py:343-354); migration 28 added origin NOT NULL DEFAULT 'staff' and department (migrations.py:4319-4410).
- forecast_service.get_appointments (:996-1069) scopes a pure outpatient's booked row by the APPOINTMENT's department, no time window.
- Defects: cancel/complete not ward-scoped (appointments_routes.py:476-598); /mine (:423), _validate_slot (:133-160), _validate_date_only and default_slot_for use the server's date.today()/datetime.now(). Booking needs patient.write (:323-345). Portal slots hard-coded (PatientShell.tsx:86-94). opd_visits.appointment_id stored, never read.

READMISSION HAZARDS (no patient in the dev DB has more than one admission, so none is exercised)
- Discharge flips patients/admissions status but leaves medications.status 'active' (emar_service.py:585-613); the eMAR's only guard is patients.status 'admitted'. Readmitting onto the same row would make the previous stay's drugs administrable again.
- No uniqueness on one active admission per patient. patient_profiles has patient_id as PRIMARY KEY (database.py:93). discharge_summaries has no admission_id (database.py:190-198); /vigil/discharged LEFT JOINs it (vigil_routes.py:489-506), so a twice-discharged patient lists twice.
- 15 readers fetch a patient's case room by patient_id with no ORDER BY (bot_service, bridge_service:166, helix_service:423, ingestion_service:362, sage_handoff_service:541,596, surgery_service:455 and others).
- NABH inpatient-days (nabh_service.py:1321-1330) and the shadow scorecard (shadow_scorecard_service.py:1642-1700) derive stays from patients.admission_date plus MAX(discharged_at) and read every patients row.

TERMINOLOGY
- terminology_service seeds a small curated ICD-10 list (:121); validate_code is an exact lookup. The docstring names scripts/load_terminology.py, but that file does not exist anywhere in the repo.

BILLING
- The Charges picker reads /vigil/patients plus /vigil/discharged only (BillingPanel.tsx:711-737). POST /api/billing/patients/{id}/opd-invoice exists (billing_routes.py:528-560) and src/api/billing.ts:433 already wraps it as createOpdInvoice, but no screen calls it.

FLAGS
- Hospital modules default ON via config._module_enabled (config.py:620-648), documented as never gating a clinical path; published on /api/health. The client cache defaults every module to true (shellConfig.tsx:249-253). CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS is pinned to ['dietary'] (shellConfig.tsx:825, shellConfig.test.ts:328). There is no default-off flag mechanism.

RETENTION
- consent_service._RETENTION_SOURCES (:646-680) is review-only: Orb destroys nothing on a timer (:882-889) and there is no clinical_record erasure executor (_ERASURE_EXECUTORS, :1061).

MIGRATIONS: highest is 47 (vitals_carried_from, migrations.py:5446-5495).

0. RESPONSE TO THE CRITIQUE (each issue re-checked against the code)
1. Blocker, the OPD arm opens write routes: ACCEPTED. require_patient_access is one guard for reads and writes, and medication add and nurse obs have no status check. Fix: patient_in_scope, scope_patient_ids_sql and PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL are NOT changed. The OPD arm is a separate opt-in predicate, permissions.patient_in_opd_scope, reached only through require_patient_access(..., opd_arm=True) or enforce_patient_scope(..., opd_arm=True) on a short whitelist. Every existing chart route, read or write, stays admission-only, and a drift test pins the whitelist.
2. No allergy capture in OPD: ACCEPTED. New increment opd-10a (allergy review plus an assessment status) and new ruling OPD-S7.
3. Registration record routes hospital-wide: ACCEPTED. Only the minimal-field search is hospital-wide. Record, changes, card and PATCH use require_patient_access(..., opd_arm=True); only an account with no department reads hospital-wide. The drift-guard exempt set stays empty.
4. Admin widening: ACCEPTED. opd.consult goes to doctor and clinician only. Admin gets registration.read (admin already reads hospital-wide through patient.read_all) and schedule.manage (configuration, no PHI). registration.write for admin is folded into OPD-N3 and not granted by default.
5. Self-granted access: ACCEPTED in substance. With fix 1 a self-registered visit can no longer reach the inpatient chart, FHIR export or any chart write. What remains (the OPD record view) is controlled: the visit that opens scope writes an in-transaction clinical_access row 'opd_scope_opened', flagged self_registered when the registrant holds opd.consult. OPD-N2 now asks whether such visits open scope at all and how far the record view reaches.
6. Discharged patient into another clinic: ACCEPTED. When OPD_ENABLED, opd_registration_allowed allows any patient with no ACTIVE admission; flag off is unchanged.
7. Matcher blind outside registration: ACCEPTED. Keys move to a self-healing side table, patient_match_keys, re-synced for any row whose source fields changed before every match, so no writer (admission, Scribe, importers, seeds) can leave a patient invisible. The admission doors run the hard match and honour ORB_UHID_SOURCE in new increment opd-5b, after the Scribe session lands.
8. opd-17 undersized: ACCEPTED, and the risk is larger than stated. Discharge leaves medications 'active', so readmission onto the same row reopens the last stay's drugs on the eMAR. Split into opd-17a (registered to inpatient), opd-17b (stay keying) and opd-17c (readmit a discharged patient), with new ruling OPD-S8.
9. Sage parity: ACCEPTED as a defect of the old design, and resolved by fix 1. The parity test and the sage_routes provenance lane stay exactly as they are. The OPD tab hides the Sage assistant and never publishes a patient into ActiveViewContext.
10. Forecast regression: ACCEPTED. forecast_service is not touched by opd-7; the appointment's own department keeps scoping the appointment row.
11. ICD-10: ACCEPTED. Diagnoses are free text with an optional code and a code_status, and an unknown code is stored as unvalidated, not refused. Correction to the critique: scripts/load_terminology.py does not exist. A loader is opd-20, behind licence ruling OPD-N11.
12. Kiosk and socket: ACCEPTED. The board uses a per-board device key (no user account, no PHI). Doctors hold vitals.read, so the nudge to dept rooms reaches them through ws.realtime.schedule_on_loop with no realtime.py edit. Desk accounts get an opd room in opd-9b after the CORS session merges. Until then the desk polls every 30 s at a stated audit cost, and dedupe is ruling OPD-N12.
13. Permission wiring: ACCEPTED. A new require_registration_desk(mode) dependency does not hang off patient.read_all. /start and /complete move to opd.consult when OPD_ENABLED. Receptionist booking is settled in opd-16.
14. Frontend role files: ACCEPTED, added to opd-3. admin_users_routes.ALLOWED_ROLES already derives from roles.STORABLE_ROLES (admin_users_routes.py:58), so it needs no edit.
15. Unfiltered readers: ACCEPTED. The shadow scorecard and NABH inpatient-days exclude never-admitted rows in opd-2. orb_patients_total counting registered rows matches its label ("patient records"), so it stays, with a test that pins orb_active_admissions.
16. Placeholder UHID series: ACCEPTED. Orb-mode registration refuses until the series is configured.
17. LWBS and charging: ACCEPTED. LWBS is a cancel with reason code left_without_being_seen and no charge. A cancel voids a registration-time charge through billing_service.cancel_charge.
18. AST guard over-claim: ACCEPTED. A dedicated guard, test_opd_no_scoring.py.
19. Migration details: ACCEPTED for the appointments rebuild (orphan pre-check, migration 28 columns, both indexes) and for registering the new tables in _RETENTION_SOURCES. PARTLY REJECTED on retention triggers. Retention is review-only and there is no clinical_record erasure executor, so there is no conflict today. A future signed-destruction executor must use a documented trigger bypass, as audit_logs would.
20. Rulings under-gated: ACCEPTED. IDs are prefixed OPD-. opd-5, opd-5b, opd-7, opd-10a and opd-19 are gated. OPD-S6, S7 and S8 and OPD-N11 and N12 are added.
21. Config conventions and dates: ACCEPTED. A separate FEATURE_FLAGS map, and every appointment date check moves to hospital_time in opd-16.

1. PRINCIPLES
- Extend what exists: frontdesk_service and opd_visits, the billing spine, the ABDM rails, orders, admission_service, clinical_records_service.record_allergies_on.
- No parallel patient table and no fourth medication store. patients.mrn is the UHID.
- The OPD arm is opt-in and narrow. Existing chart routes never see it.
- OPD never computes or shows NEWS2, a band or AI advice (R023 and the Ward Record no-score rule), enforced by a dedicated AST guard.
- No AI model anywhere in the identity lane.
- Every handler is a plain def. Every patient_id arrives in a typed body or the path. target_id is always a string.

2. FEATURE FLAGS (server/config.py)
- A new FEATURE_FLAGS block, separate from HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV and documented as the opposite convention: default OFF, and allowed to gate clinical paths. _feature_enabled(env) is on only for 1/true/yes/on.
- REGISTRATION_ENABLED = ORB_REGISTRATION.
- OPD_ENABLED = ORB_OPD and REGISTRATION_ENABLED and FRONTDESK_ENABLED. If a prerequisite is missing, the boot log names it.
- Settings:
  - ORB_UHID_SOURCE: hospital|orb, default hospital.
  - ORB_UHID_PATTERN: optional regex.
  - ORB_OPD_SCOPE_DAYS: default 7.
  - ORB_OPD_CHARGE_AT: completion|registration, default completion.
  - ORB_DUPLICATE_MODE: warn|block. Read only after OPD-S2 is ruled; until then registration refuses to start if it is unset with REGISTRATION_ENABLED.
  - ORB_OPD_QUEUE_POLL_SECONDS: 30.
- feature_flags() is published on /api/health as a separate 'features' object. enabled_modules() is unchanged.
- Client (src/shellConfig.tsx): FeatureFlagId = 'registration'|'opd', and DEFAULT_FEATURE_FLAGS are all false, so an unrefreshed cache fails toward hidden. The OPD tab is a feature tab with its own panel lookup, NOT a HospitalModuleId. HOSPITAL_MODULE_IDS, DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS and the CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS pin are untouched.
- Every new route 404s when its flag is off (require_registration_feature, require_opd_feature).
- With flags off, the only differences are: the additive migrations, the patients CHECK rebuild, the users role rebuild, the stay-keying migration, the retired ghost route (410), and the duplicate-MRN 500 becoming 409.
- Other epics need the same mechanism. Whichever lands first builds FEATURE_FLAGS; the others only add ids.

3. DATA MODEL
Version numbers are provisional (next free after 47 at merge). No foreign keys; money in _paise (migration 20 rules).

- M48 registration_opd_foundation (additive)
  a. Frozen opd_visits and patient_movements DDL and indexes, so later ALTERs never precede the lazy CREATE.
  b. opd_visits ADD:
     - queue: priority DEFAULT 'normal', priority_reason, room, arrival_source DEFAULT 'walk_in', checked_in_at, call_count DEFAULT 0, skipped_at
     - outcome: disposition (home|follow_up|referred_internal|referred_external|admitted), disposition_at, admission_id, follow_up_of_visit_id, cancel_reason_code (incl. left_without_being_seen)
     - links: session_id, payer_id, tariff_plan_id, registration_charge_id
     - control: identity_check_json, scope_self_registered DEFAULT 0
  c. admissions ADD opd_visit_id. orders ADD opd_visit_id (indexed).
  d. document_number_series ADD resets_yearly DEFAULT 1 and check_digit. Seed a UHID row: resets_yearly 0, verhoeff, is_configured 0.
  e. patient_demographics, one row per patient:
     - provenance: registered_at, registered_by, registration_source (desk|admission|scribe|import|er), uhid_source
     - age_recorded_on (a stated age is never turned into a DOB)
     - guardian_relation, guardian_name, marital_status, preferred_language
     - address_line, city, district, state_code, pin_code, alt_phone, email
     - id_document_type, id_document_last4, occupation
     - row_version, updated_at, updated_by
     patients itself gets NO new columns, so the M49 rebuild column list is only what exists today.
  f. patient_identity_changes, append-only (UPDATE and DELETE blocked by triggers): field, old_value, new_value, reason NOT NULL, changed_by, changed_at, correlation_id.
  g. patient_duplicate_candidates: the pair (unique), score, reasons_json, status (open|not_duplicate|confirmed_duplicate|merged), source (registration|admission|sweep|import), resolver and timestamps.
  h. patient_match_keys: patient_id PK, name_key, phone_key, dob, sex, src_name, src_phone, src_dob, src_sex, normalizer_version, computed_at. name_key and phone_key are indexed.
  i. opd_display_boards: id, department, label, key_hash, created_by/at, revoked_by/at.
  j. consent_service._RETENTION_SOURCES clinical_record gains opd_visits, patient_demographics, patient_identity_changes and patient_match_keys.

- M49 patients_status_registered
  - FK-parent rebuild through database._atomic_table_rebuild (the m33 users shape), widening the CHECK to add 'registered'.
  - Frozen canonical column list; post_sql recreates the patients indexes; aborts on unknown columns or objects.
  - database.SCHEMA is updated, with a parity test.
  - 'registered' means on the index and never admitted. A discharged patient seen in OPD stays 'discharged'.
  - Batch the adt and death-record statuses into this one rebuild.

- M50 users_role_receptionist: _rebuild_users_role_check plus LATEST_USERS_ROLE_CHECK, batched with every other epic's new roles.

- M51 opd_consultations, one per visit:
  - fields: author; status draft|signed; chief_complaint, history, examination
  - vitals_json: values, measured_at, measured_by
  - diagnoses_json: items {text, code_system, code, code_status validated|unvalidated|none}
  - plan, advice, follow_up_date, follow_up_note, referral_department, admission_advised
  - control: row_version, signed_by/at
  Plus opd_consultation_addenda (append-only). Both are registered in retention.

- M52 patient_allergy_assessments, append-only: patient_id; status none_known|allergies_recorded|unable_to_obtain; opd_visit_id; admission_id; assessed_by/at; note. Registered in retention.

- M53 opd_charge_rules: department, doctor_id, visit_type, service_code, follow_up_window_days, is_active.

- M54 clinic_sessions and clinic_session_exceptions.

- M55 appointments_slots: in-transaction rebuild of appointments (not an FK parent).
  - Pre-check orphan patient_id and booked_by_user_id values and abort with a list.
  - Carry origin NOT NULL DEFAULT 'staff' and department; recreate idx_appointments_patient and idx_appointments_idem.
  - Add the statuses checked_in and no_show; add doctor_id, session_id, checked_in_at, opd_visit_id, no_show_at, cancel_reason, cancelled_by, rescheduled_from_id.
  - Partial unique index on live (doctor_id, scheduled_date, scheduled_time), pre-checked for clashes.

- M56 stay_keying (additive):
  - discharge_summaries ADD admission_id, backfilled where the patient has exactly one admission.
  - CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_admissions_one_active ON admissions(patient_id) WHERE status='active', after a pre-check that aborts listing violators.

4. SERVICES
- registration_service.py (new): register_patient, search_index, get_registration, correct_demographics, change_history, check_identity, find_candidates, resolve_duplicate.
  - UHID, hospital mode: the site pattern plus uniqueness (exact and normalised).
  - UHID, orb mode: billing_masters.allocate_series_number(db,'UHID'), using the caller's handle, no yearly reset, Verhoeff check digit. Refused with 409 'uhid_series_not_configured' until the series is configured.
  - One immediate transaction writes:
    - patients: status 'registered', admission_date NULL, no portal login, no allergy field;
    - patient_demographics;
    - patient_match_keys;
    - the ABHA placeholder via abdm_service.record_abha_on(db, ...), always unverified;
    - the audit row.
  - check_identity compares the identifiers the patient states (DOB or stated age, phone last 4, UHID) and answers only match or no match. It never returns stored values. Five failures per user per patient per hour returns 429, and failures are audited.
- patient_matching.py (new, deterministic):
  - normalizers: honorific strip, Indian transliteration folds, phone to 10 digits
  - keys_for(row)
  - sync_keys(db): an indexed LEFT JOIN finds rows with no key row, changed source fields or an old normalizer_version, and recomputes them. It runs before every match, so any writer is covered.
  - score: hard matches on exact UHID or active ABHA; points for phone (+40), name (+40 exact key, +25 token overlap), DOB (+30 exact, +10 age within 2 years), sex (-20 on mismatch); bands probable 70 or more, possible 50 to 69.
- frontdesk_service (extend):
  - queue actions call, skip, recall, assign and priority/room; doctor queue; board snapshot
  - disposition on completion; LWBS as a cancel with no charge
  - charge codes from opd_charge_rules
  - in OPD mode: register, start, complete and cancel audits written in-transaction, and the visit that opens scope writes 'opd_scope_opened'
  - opd_registration_allowed: in OPD mode, any patient with no ACTIVE admission
  - ensure_frontdesk_schema kept in step with M48
- opd_service.py (new):
  - OPD record composer
  - consultation draft/save/sign/addendum/history
  - allergy review: record_allergies_on plus an assessment row in one transaction
  - visit-scoped orders through orders_service.create_order(opd_visit_id=...)
  - never writes vitals, risk_scores or medications, and never scores
- clinic_schedule_service.py (new): sessions, exceptions, availability in hospital-local time.
- admission_service (extend, after the Scribe session lands): door checks (opd-5b) and admit_existing_patient (opd-17a, opd-17c).
- discharge_service (opd-17b): writes admission_id on the summary.
- permissions (extend): patient_in_opd_scope, the opd_arm keyword, require_registration_desk.

5. ROUTES
- /api/registration (ORB_REGISTRATION; require_registration_desk):
  - GET config: UHID mode, series configured, ABDM on.
  - GET search: hospital-wide minimal fields (UHID, name, sex, age, phone last 4, last visit date, inpatient now yes/no). Minimum 3 characters, 20 results, phi_access with the matched ids.
  - POST match, POST patients.
  - GET and PATCH patients/{patient_id}, GET patients/{patient_id}/changes, GET patients/{patient_id}/card: require_patient_access(REGISTRATION_READ or REGISTRATION_WRITE, opd_arm=True, audit_action=...).
  - GET duplicates; POST duplicates/{id}/resolve (registration.write; the resolver must not be the person who overrode).
- /api/frontdesk/opd:
  - POST visits gains identity_check, required when the patient was picked from search (per OPD-S1).
  - New in OPD mode: POST visits/{id}/call, skip, recall and assign; PATCH visits/{id}; cancel with a reason code.
  - /start and /complete need opd.consult when OPD_ENABLED.
  - POST and DELETE boards (schedule.manage). GET board takes the X-Orb-Board-Key header and no user token.
  - GET appointments/day, GET mis/daily.
- /api/opd (ORB_OPD; opd.consult):
  - GET my-queue
  - GET patients/{patient_id}/record and GET patients/{patient_id}/consultations (opd_arm=True, audited)
  - GET/PUT visits/{visit_id}/consultation, POST .../sign, POST .../addenda
  - POST visits/{visit_id}/allergy-review, POST visits/{visit_id}/complete
  - POST visits/{visit_id}/orders
  - POST visits/{visit_id}/prescriptions (after medorder-1)
  - GET terminology/search
- /api/schedule: sessions, exceptions, availability.
- /api/appointments: doctor and slot booking, reschedule, check-in, no-show, plus the scope and date fixes.
- POST /api/admissions/admit-existing. GET /api/billing/op-patients.

6. PERMISSIONS, ROLES AND SCOPE
- roles.py adds 'receptionist'. The department is optional: blank means a central desk that sees every clinic. It is not in DEPARTMENT_REQUIRED_ROLES.
- New permissions: registration.read, registration.write, opd.consult, schedule.manage.
- Grants:
  - doctor and clinician: registration.read, registration.write, opd.consult.
  - admin: registration.read and schedule.manage. registration.write only if OPD-N3 says so.
  - receptionist: registration.read and registration.write; consent.record only per OPD-N3.
  - nurse, pharmacist and cashier: unchanged.
- require_registration_desk(mode), with an audited denial and the feature switch:
  - read: patient.read_all OR registration.read.
  - write: frontdesk.write OR patient.write OR registration.write.
  - Used by desk reads, the doctors list, visit register and cancel, and the registration routes.
  - Transfers keep require_frontdesk_write (patient.read_all base), so a receptionist cannot transfer.
- Call, skip, recall, assign, start, complete and consultation need opd.consult. OPD Rx needs opd.consult AND medication.prescribe (today's prescriber-only permission; decides nothing on R010).
- OPD arm: patient_in_opd_scope(db, pid, dept) is true when any of these holds:
  - dept is None;
  - patient_in_scope is true;
  - OPD_ENABLED, AND the patient has no ACTIVE admission, AND a non-cancelled opd_visits row in dept (case-folded) has visit_date on or after hospital_today minus ORB_OPD_SCOPE_DAYS.
  It is reachable ONLY through opd_arm=True. Whitelist, each with its reason in test_opd_scope_drift.py:
  - GET /api/opd/patients/{patient_id}/record and /consultations;
  - GET and PATCH /api/registration/patients/{patient_id}, /changes and /card;
  - the staff branch of POST /api/appointments (from opd-16).
- Visit-scoped /api/opd/visits/{visit_id}/... routes use _visit_or_404. Writes there refuse when the patient now has an active admission.
- Sage is untouched: parity holds, and provenance stays admission-only.

7. UI
- Front Desk tab (admin and receptionist):
  - Register view, search first.
  - Identity dialog: the desk types what the patient states and the server answers match or no match. The stored DOB is never shown.
  - Duplicate warnings need a reason (in the OPD-S2 mode).
  - Demographics drawer with reasoned correction and change history.
  - ABHA placeholder labelled unverified.
  - DOB or stated age, with the R018 hint.
  - Prints: UHID card (Code128 as SVG) and token slip.
  - Queue shows priority, room and skipped, and has an LWBS action.
  - Further views: Appointments day, Clinic timings, Day summary, Display boards.
- OPD tab (OpdPanel, feature tab, doctor and clinician rails only):
  - Panels: my queue, add walk-in (the same register component), and the record view.
  - The record view shows identity, allergies with their status ('not yet asked' or 'no known allergies, asked by X on date'), problems, OPD-linked results and consultations.
  - Consultation editor and allergy review. Vitals are typed with their time and shown with no colour, no band and no score.
  - Diagnoses are free text plus an optional code; investigations; Rx after medorder; disposition; sign and print.
  - It never links an outpatient to the Vigil chart. It hides SageFloatingAssistant and never calls setViewSelection with a patientId.
- Kiosk /display/opd#key=... reads the key from the URL fragment and sends it as a header.
- Receptionist rail: Front Desk only. AdmitPatientModal gets an existing-patient mode. The Billing picker includes outpatients, and the OPD counter form uses createOpdInvoice.
- House design rules apply: no opacity, status tokens, modals portal to body, contrast gate, no em dashes, no demo wording.

8. AUDIT
- New fail-closed category 'patient_identity', written in-transaction: patient_registered, patient_demographics_corrected, patient_uhid_corrected (admin only), registration_duplicate_override, duplicate_resolved, identity_check_failed.
- clinical_access, in-transaction: opd_scope_opened (with self_registered), opd_converted_to_admission, patient_readmitted, previous_stay_medications_closed.
- phi_access: patient_index_searched (matched ids), registration_record_viewed, registration_changes_viewed, uhid_card_printed, opd_record_viewed, opd_consultation_viewed, op_patients_listed, and opd_queue_viewed (every non-empty read until OPD-N12).
- clinical_record: queue actions; consultation saved, signed (in-transaction) and addendum; allergy review (in-transaction); visit completed with disposition; appointment rescheduled, checked_in and no_show.
- configuration: sessions, charge rules, board keys.
- The socket and the board carry no PHI.
- Cost: a desk polling at 30 s writes up to 1,200 phi_access rows per open desk screen per 10-hour day until opd-9b.

9. LINKS TO OTHER EPICS
- adt: the bed picker for conversion; one patients-status rebuild; admission_service ownership agreed (admit_existing_patient and bed allocation are one design).
- medorder: OPD Rx is an outpatient-setting order in the single store, screened by enforce_medication_safety(entry_point='opd_prescription'). It never writes medications or helix rows.
- lis: OPD investigations are orders tagged opd_visit_id; results come through lis-1.
- site: the UHID series is group-wide; site_id arrives with site-1.
- ABDM: the placeholder only.
- workforce: leave becomes a session exception, later.
- Ward Record: shares the identity core (role batch, hospital-number mode, opd-5b, opd-17b and opd-17c are its 'returning patient reopens the same record').

product_rulings.question: OPD-S1 (new, patient safety): before the desk attaches a visit, or a clinician attaches an admission, to an EXISTING record found by search, which identifiers must be confirmed, and how?
product_rulings.options: (a) two identifiers the patient states (name plus DOB or stated age, plus phone last 4 or UHID), checked by the server, which answers match or no match and never shows the stored DOB, recorded in the audit; (b) UHID alone; (c) a name match alone
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Wrong-patient selection attaches someone else's allergies and history, and showing the stored DOB to a hospital-wide searcher would leak the discharge-link second factor. This also governs the Ward Record clerk's returning-patient screen.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S2 (new, patient safety): when registration or an admission door finds a probable duplicate, should the server warn or block?
product_rulings.options: (a) warn, require a reason, audit it and open a worklist item; hard refusal only on exact UHID or active ABHA; (b) block above the threshold until a supervisor reviews; (c) warn only, no reason
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Duplicate charts split the allergy history, but blocking a sick walk-in at the counter is worse.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S3 (new, patient safety, the analogue of held W111; does not decide W111): do vitals taken in OPD enter the observation chart and count as the latest vitals after conversion?
product_rulings.options: (a) no: they stay inside the OPD record, are shown on the admission form with their time, and the ward charts a fresh set; (b) copy them into vitals at conversion
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Otherwise hours-old OPD values become the board's latest reading and its NEWS2.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S4 (new, patient safety, related to held R010): do active OPD prescriptions carry onto the inpatient medication chart at conversion?
product_rulings.options: (a) never automatically: listed as OPD or home medicines for item-by-item reconciliation by the admitting prescriber; (b) carry them as active inpatient orders
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The eMAR would otherwise offer a nurse a take-home prescription as an inpatient dose.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S5 (new, patient safety): may the front desk record allergies or 'no known allergies' at registration?
product_rulings.options: (a) no allergy field at the desk; a clinician records allergies at consultation or admission; (b) the desk may record allergies but never NKDA; (c) the desk records both
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), which is how opd-4 is built. A clerk-typed NKDA would silence the interlock.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S6 (new, patient safety, related to held R023): does an abnormal vital typed into an OPD consultation prompt anyone?
product_rulings.options: (a) no automatic prompt: the value is shown with its time to the consulting doctor who typed it; (b) a fixed plain-text red-flag line for values outside fixed limits (for example SpO2 below 90), no score and no band; (c) (b) plus an automatic Relay post to an emergency responder
product_rulings.recommendation: (a) for now, because in this design only the consulting doctor enters OPD vitals and is the person who acts on them, and any automatic rule is decision-support wording that R023 governs. Revisit before any triage-nurse vitals entry is built.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S7 (new, patient safety): how is 'asked, no known allergies' recorded, and may an OPD prescription be written when the patient's allergy status was never assessed?
product_rulings.options: (a) a prescriber records an allergy review (allergies charted, 'none known', or 'unable to obtain' with a reason); signing a consultation and writing an OPD prescription are refused until one exists; (b) allowed with a visible 'allergies not yet asked' warning acknowledged in the order; (c) allowed as today
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The interlock cannot tell NKDA from never asked (allergy_interlock.py:360-366), and an OPD prescription leaves the building with nobody else checking it. The assessment never changes how the interlock screens.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S8 (new, patient safety): when a discharged patient is readmitted onto the same record, what happens to medication rows from the earlier stay that are still 'active' or 'prn'?
product_rulings.options: (a) the readmission transaction discontinues them, audited, and lists them on the admission form for item-by-item re-prescribing; (b) discontinue them at discharge instead (changes discharge for every patient); (c) leave them active
product_rulings.recommendation: (a) now, and consider (b) later as its own discharge change. Discharge leaves medications 'active' and the eMAR's only guard is patients.status 'admitted' (emar_service.py:604-613), so without this every old drug becomes administrable again on readmission.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N1: where does the UHID come from at each site, and in what format?
product_rulings.options: hospital mode (type the existing HIS number, site regex); orb mode (Orb series with a Verhoeff check digit, site prefix)
product_rulings.recommendation: Hospital mode by default (beside-HIS, Ward Record); orb mode with a check digit for a site Orb replaces; never reset per year; orb mode refused until the series is configured.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N2: how far does an OPD visit open the patient's record to that clinic, for how long, and does a visit the reader registered themselves count?
product_rulings.options: Window: same day, 7 days, 30 days. Extent: (i) identity, allergies, problems, OPD-linked results and this clinic's consultations; (ii) plus other clinics' signed consultations; (iii) plus earlier inpatient discharge summaries. Self-registered visits: (x) count, flagged and audited; (y) count only after someone else checks the patient in
product_rulings.recommendation: 7 days, extent (ii), self-registered (x). The inpatient chart, chart writes and FHIR export stay admission-only whatever is chosen. (iii) only through the existing inpatient scope until a clinician asks for it.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N3: create a receptionist role; should it also take consent (F123) and money; and should admin hold registration.write?
product_rulings.options: receptionist with registration only; plus consent.record; plus payments.record. Admin: registration.read only, or also registration.write
product_rulings.recommendation: Receptionist with registration.read and registration.write, plus consent.record once counsel agrees. Money stays with the cashier role. Admin keeps registration.read only; registering patients is the desk's and the doctor's job.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N4: may a ward-scoped account search the whole patient index (minimal fields) to avoid duplicate registrations?
product_rulings.options: yes, minimal fields, audited; no, own department only
product_rulings.recommendation: Yes: UHID, name, sex, age, phone last 4, last visit date and 'inpatient now' only; minimum 3 characters, 20 results, every search audited with the matched ids. The full record stays scoped.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N5 (existing R018): must the desk capture date of birth?
product_rulings.options: required; optional with stated age
product_rulings.recommendation: Optional, with stated age stored with its date and the 'no date of birth, no discharge link' hint. Never store an estimated DOB.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N6: when is the consultation fee charged, and is there a registration fee or free follow-up window?
product_rulings.options: at registration (prepaid) or at completion (today); REG-FEE yes or no; follow-up window in days
product_rulings.recommendation: Site setting, default completion. A follow-up window maps to its own OPD-FOLLOWUP code the site prices, never an implicit zero. Cancel and LWBS void a pending prepaid line.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N7: what does the waiting-room token board show?
product_rulings.options: token only; token and initials; token and name
product_rulings.recommendation: Token, doctor and room only (DPDP), on a per-board device key.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N8: may a visit be completed without a signed consultation note?
product_rulings.options: signed note required; allowed with a reason ('note on paper')
product_rulings.recommendation: Allowed with a reason, because many clinics will keep paper notes at first.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N9: which queue priority categories apply?
product_rulings.options: none; senior citizen, pregnant, differently abled, emergency; site list
product_rulings.recommendation: A site-configured list with a reason captured, shown on the doctor's queue.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N10: what identity document data may registration store?
product_rulings.options: none; type plus last 4; full number
product_rulings.recommendation: Type plus last 4, never a full Aadhaar number; counsel to confirm.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N11 (new): which diagnosis code list does OPD load, and under what licence?
product_rulings.options: WHO ICD-10 under a WHO licence; another release; free text with the curated seed only
product_rulings.recommendation: Free text plus optional code now (opd-10 works without a load). Counsel to confirm the licence terms of the chosen ICD-10 release before opd-20 loads it.

product_rulings.question: OPD-N12 (new): may an unchanged OPD queue re-read skip writing a new phi_access row?
product_rulings.options: (a) audit every non-empty read (today); (b) one row per user per distinct set of visible visits per 10 minutes, with the visit ids in metadata
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). The disclosure is identical, and polling desks would otherwise write about 1,200 rows per screen per day, while audit already drives appliance storage.

risks: The patients rebuild (opd-2) is an FK-parent rebuild under about 35 child tables, done in an autocommit window that commits the runner's earlier work. It runs on every install, Ward Record included, even with the flags off. A defect here loses or orphans patient rows. Mitigations: the proven _atomic_table_rebuild path, a frozen column list (M48 deliberately adds no patients columns), row-count and foreign_key_check assertions, a verified backup first, and a dry run on a dev DB copy on an isolated verify stack.

Readmission onto the same record (opd-17c, and the Ward Record returning patient) reopens the previous stay's still-active medications on the eMAR unless OPD-S8 is ruled and built. That is the sharpest hazard in this epic. Stay-keyed readers beyond the ones listed may surface later, which is why opd-17b includes a written reader audit.

Every new role is a users rebuild (FK parent of about 20 tables), and its canonical column list is hard-coded. Batch receptionist, the Ward Record clerk and other epics' roles into one migration, and any epic adding a users column must update the list in the same change.

Migration version collisions: about ten sessions and several epic architects will claim numbers after 47, and a duplicate schema_migrations key stops the server from booting. Reserve a block per epic (this epic needs 9: M48 to M56).

The OPD arm still widens reads. A wrong window, a forgotten no-active-admission rule, or an opd_arm=True added to a chart route would reopen the 2026-08-05 class. Mitigations: an opt-in kwarg, a whitelist drift test, explicit 404 tests on the high-risk writes, and the flag held off until OPD-N2 is ruled.

Opt-in scope means an OPD doctor cannot see a returning patient's inpatient history from another ward (for example a recent discharge summary) unless OPD-N2 widens the extent. That is a continuity gap traded for privacy, and it should be stated to the clinical champion.

Wrong-patient selection at returning-patient search and split duplicate charts both lose allergy history (OPD-S1, OPD-S2, OPD-S5, OPD-S7). The stated-identifier check is an oracle, so it is rate-limited and audited.

patient_match_keys is a second encrypted copy of name, phone, DOB and sex. That widens the DPDP footprint. It is classified clinical_record and must be included in any future erasure or merge executor.

Self-healing key sync scans patients with a LEFT JOIN before each match. At 100k+ rows in SQLCipher this may be slow; opd-5 measures it and can fall back to a bounded incremental sync. FTS5 availability in sqlcipher3-wheels is unverified.
Audit volume: until opd-9b, each open desk screen polling at 30 s writes up to 1,200 phi_access rows a day (OPD-N12 would cut this). Doctors refetch on nudge only.
OPD prescription depends on medorder-1. The shortcut of writing OPD prescriptions into medications would put take-home drugs on the eMAR; a test forbids it.
ICD-10 coverage: the seed is small and the loader does not exist. Free-text diagnoses keep the note usable, but coded reporting (MIS, NABH, ABDM) waits for opd-20 and the licence answer.

Default-off FEATURE_FLAGS is new cross-epic infrastructure. If two epics each build their own mechanism, the client will end up with two caches and two conventions. Agree that the first epic to land owns it.

Lane competition: about 84 engineer-days, about 95 with browser re-verification and merge friction, which is about 24 weeks at the sales plan's 4 engineer-days a week. It competes with the Ward Record build (28 to 44.5 days), the only paid product. The minimum useful slice (walk-in to billed consultation: opd-1, 2, 3, 7, 4, 5, 6a, 8, 10, 10a, 11, 13, 14) is about 45 days and needs OPD-S1, OPD-S2, OPD-S7 and OPD-N2 ruled before it can be switched on.

Defects found while mapping, outside any running session: appointment cancel and complete are not ward-scoped; appointment dates use the server clock; the ghost POST /api/vigil/patients is live; front-desk OPD audits are written after commit in a fail-soft category. The first three are worth a quick fix before opd-16 and opd-1 land.

Device class: OPD screens must never show NEWS2, a band or AI advice (R023, the Ward Record rule). OPD vitals stay in the OPD record, the dedicated AST guard covers the new modules, and the OPD tab hides Sage.
Prescription and consultation prints need the doctor's qualification, which Orb does not store. Until credentialing adds it, prints carry only the name and users.registration_number.

first_draft.design:
PRINCIPLES
- Extend what exists: frontdesk_service and opd_visits, the billing spine, the ABDM rails, orders, admission_service.
- No parallel patient table and no fourth medication store.
- patients.mrn is the UHID.
- OPD never computes or shows NEWS2 or any score. This follows R023 and the Ward Record rule, and the existing AST guard enforces it.
- No AI model anywhere in the identity lane.
- Every handler is a plain def, and every patient_id arrives in a typed body or the path.

1. FEATURE FLAGS (server/config.py, following the ORB_* module pattern)
- New helper _flag_default_off(env): on only for 1/true/yes/on.
- REGISTRATION_ENABLED = ORB_REGISTRATION (default off).
- OPD_ENABLED = ORB_OPD AND REGISTRATION_ENABLED AND FRONTDESK_ENABLED. Default off; the boot log says which prerequisite is missing.
- Settings:
  - ORB_UHID_SOURCE = hospital|orb (default hospital, the beside-HIS case).
  - ORB_UHID_PATTERN: optional regex for hospital numbers.
  - ORB_OPD_SCOPE_DAYS: default 7.
  - ORB_OPD_CHARGE_AT = completion|registration (default completion, which is today's behaviour).
  - ORB_DUPLICATE_MODE = warn|block (default warn).
- enabled_modules() adds "registration" and "opd", published on /api/health.
- Client (src/shellConfig.tsx):
  - 'opd' becomes a HospitalModuleId with panel ./pages/panels/OpdPanel.tsx.
  - 'registration' becomes a separate non-tab FeatureFlagId.
  - Both default false in the client cache.
- Every new route 404s when its flag is off (the require_frontdesk_module pattern).
- With both flags off, the Ward Record profile and the demos see no new route, tab or behaviour. The only differences are the additive and rebuild migrations and the retired ghost route.

2. DATA MODEL
Numbers are provisional (next free after 47 at merge time). No foreign keys and money in _paise, per the migration 20 rules.

- M48 registration_opd_foundation (additive)
  a. Fold the front-desk tables into the ledger: a frozen copy of the opd_visits and patient_movements DDL and indexes (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS). Without this, on a fresh DB the ALTERs below would run before the lazy CREATE and be skipped forever.
  b. opd_visits ADD:
     - queue: priority DEFAULT 'normal', priority_reason, room, arrival_source DEFAULT 'walk_in', checked_in_at, call_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, skipped_at
     - outcome: disposition (home|follow_up|referred_internal|referred_external|admitted|lwbs), disposition_at, admission_id, follow_up_of_visit_id
     - links: session_id, payer_id, tariff_plan_id, registration_charge_id
     Enums are validated in the service.
  c. patients ADD:
     - provenance: registered_at, registered_by, registration_source, uhid_source
     - age_recorded_on: DOB is never estimated, because it is the discharge-link second factor.
     - match keys: name_key and phone_key, each indexed, backfilled with a frozen v1 normalizer.
  d. admissions ADD opd_visit_id; orders ADD opd_visit_id (indexed).
  e. document_number_series ADD resets_yearly (DEFAULT 1) and check_digit. Seed a UHID row (resets_yearly 0, verhoeff, is_configured 0).
  f. patient_demographics, one row per patient:
     - guardian_relation, guardian_name, marital_status, preferred_language
     - address_line, city, district, state_code, pin_code, alt_phone, email
     - id_document_type, id_document_last4 (never a full Aadhaar number), occupation
     - row_version, updated_at, updated_by
  g. patient_identity_changes, append-only (triggers block UPDATE and DELETE): field, old_value, new_value, reason NOT NULL, changed_by, changed_at, correlation_id.
  h. patient_duplicate_candidates:
     - the pair (unique), score and reasons_json
     - status open|not_duplicate|confirmed_duplicate|merged; source registration|sweep|import
     - resolver and timestamps

- M49 patients_status_registered
  - Widens the CHECK to admitted|discharged|transferred|registered through database._atomic_table_rebuild (the m33 users shape), with a frozen canonical column list.
  - post_sql recreates idx_patients_import_external, idx_patients_import_run, name_key and phone_key.
  - It aborts on unknown columns or objects.
  - database.SCHEMA is updated for fresh DBs, with a parity test.
  - 'registered' means on the index and never admitted. A discharged patient seen in OPD stays 'discharged'.
  - Neither NULL nor 'admitted' is safe for an outpatient: about 20 queries filter on status='admitted' alone, and the Relay Sage context uses COALESCE(status,'admitted').

- M50 users_role_receptionist: _rebuild_users_role_check plus LATEST_USERS_ROLE_CHECK. Batch this with every other epic's new roles (for example the Ward Record clerk) into one rebuild.

- M51 opd_consultations: one per visit, author, status draft|signed. Columns:
  - content: chief_complaint, history, examination, vitals_json (values, measured_at, measured_by), diagnoses_json (text plus ICD-10), plan, advice
  - follow-up and referral: follow_up_date, follow_up_note, referral_department, admission_advised
  - control: row_version, signed_by/at
  Plus opd_consultation_addenda, append-only.

3. SERVICES
- registration_service.py (new): register_patient, search_index, get_registration, correct_demographics, change_history, find_candidates, resolve_duplicate.
  - UHID, hospital mode: the typed number is checked against the site pattern and for uniqueness, both exact and by normalised key.
  - UHID, orb mode: billing_masters.allocate_series_number(db,'UHID') (new; uses the caller's handle, no yearly reset, Verhoeff check digit).
  - One immediate transaction per registration writes:
    - the patients row: status 'registered', no portal login, no allergy field;
    - patient_demographics;
    - the ABHA placeholder through abdm_service.record_abha_on(db, ...) (new handle-taking variant, always unverified);
    - the audit row.
  - Name through patient_name_rule.validate_patient_name. Sex normalised to the dialect src/lib/demographics.ts reads. Phone normalised to 10 digits.
- patient_matching.py (new, deterministic):
  - Name folding: honorific strip (Mr/Mrs/Smt/Shri/Kumari/Dr/Baby of), Mohd to mohammed, aa/ee/oo/w/ph/sh/z folds, doubled letters.
  - Hard matches: exact UHID, or an active ABHA.
  - Points:
    - phone: +40
    - name: +40 for an exact key, +25 for token overlap
    - DOB: +30 for an exact match, +10 for age within 2 years
    - sex: -20 on mismatch
  - Bands: 70 or more is probable, 50 to 69 is possible.
- frontdesk_service (extend):
  - queue actions: call, skip, recall, assign-to-me, priority/room
  - views: the doctor's queue, a name-free board snapshot
  - completion that records a disposition
  - charge code from opd_charge_rules, with REG-FEE and OPD-FOLLOWUP items registered unpriced (never an implicit Rs 0)
  - ensure_frontdesk_schema kept in step with M48
- opd_service.py (new):
  - consultation draft with row_version, sign, addendum, history
  - ICD-10 through terminology_service.validate_code; optional problem_list add
  - never writes vitals or risk_scores, never calls scoring
- clinic_schedule_service.py (new): sessions, exceptions and availability in the hospital's local time.
- admission_service (extend, after the Scribe session lands): admit_existing_patient shares admit_patient's inserts, and a duplicate MRN on /admit becomes a 409.
- permissions (extend): an OPD arm (section 5).

- /api/frontdesk/opd (existing routes plus ORB_OPD):
  - POST visits/{id}/call|skip|recall|assign, PATCH visits/{id}
  - GET board (no PHI)
  - /api/frontdesk/appointments/day, /api/frontdesk/mis/daily
- /api/opd (ORB_OPD):
  - GET my-queue
  - GET/PUT visits/{visit_id}/consultation, POST .../sign, POST .../addenda
  - POST visits/{visit_id}/complete, POST visits/{visit_id}/orders
  - POST visits/{visit_id}/prescriptions (after medorder-1)
  - GET patients/{patient_id}/consultations (require_patient_access)
  - GET terminology/search

- /api/appointments: doctor/slot booking, reschedule, check-in (creates the OPD visit), no-show; plus the cancel/complete scope fix.
- POST /api/admissions/admit-existing.
- GET /api/billing/op-patients.

5. PERMISSIONS AND ROLES
- roles.py: add 'receptionist'. The department is optional: blank means a central desk that sees every clinic's queue; a value means that clinic only.
- New permissions in permissions.py: registration.read, registration.write, opd.consult, schedule.manage.
- Grants:
  - doctor and clinician: + registration.read, registration.write, opd.consult.
  - admin: all four.
  - receptionist: registration.read, registration.write; consent.record only if N3 says so.
  - nurse: unchanged.
- Route rules:
  - require_frontdesk_read accepts patient.read_all OR registration.read.
  - Register, cancel and check-in accept frontdesk.write OR patient.write OR registration.write.
  - Call, skip, consultation and complete-with-disposition need opd.consult.
  - Transfers are unchanged; a receptionist cannot transfer.
  - OPD Rx needs opd.consult AND medication.prescribe. That is today's prescriber-only permission, not a decision on R010.
- OPD scope arm (only when OPD_ENABLED). A patient with NO active admission is in a scoped caller's department when a non-cancelled opd_visits row in that department has visit_date on or after hospital_today minus ORB_OPD_SCOPE_DAYS.
  - It lives in patient_in_scope and scope_patient_ids_sql; PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL is unchanged.
  - The no-active-admission rule stops a front-desk visit from laundering access to another ward's inpatient.
  - Sage's duplicate scope (sage_service.py:1933) is left alone, so Sage stays admission-only, and a test says so.

6. UI (mounts in src/shellConfig.tsx)
- Front Desk tab (admin and receptionist):
  - Register view, search first: by UHID, phone, name plus DOB, or ABHA.
  - Picking an existing patient opens an identity-confirm dialog.
  - A new registration shows duplicate warnings that need a reason to override.
  - Demographics drawer with reasoned correction and change history.
  - ABHA placeholder field when ORB_ABDM is on.
  - DOB or stated age, with the R018 hint.
  - UHID card (Code128 drawn as SVG, no new dependency) and token slip.
  - Queue shows priority, room and skipped.
  - Further views: Appointments day list, Clinic timings, Day summary.
  - The visit form picks the patient from index search instead of /vigil/patients?limit=200.
- New OPD tab (OpdPanel.tsx, 'clinical' group, doctor and clinician rails only). CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS becomes ['dietary','opd'] and shellConfig.test.ts is updated with the reason.
  - My queue
  - Consultation editor: complaint, history, exam, timed OPD vitals, ICD-10 diagnoses, plan, investigations, prescription once medorder lands, advice, follow-up, referral, advise admission
  - Sign and print
- Kiosk route /display/opd (OpdTokenBoard.tsx in App.tsx): token, doctor and room only.
- Receptionist rail: home 'frontdesk', tabs [frontdesk].
- AdmitPatientModal: an existing-patient mode.
- Billing: the picker includes today's outpatients, plus an OPD counter invoice form.
- House design rules apply: no opacity, status tokens, modals portal to body, contrast gate, no em dashes, no demo wording.

7. AUDIT
- New fail-closed category 'patient_identity', added to _FAIL_CLOSED_CATEGORIES and pinned by its test. It is written in the SAME transaction via log_audit_event(db=...), so there is no mutation without audit. Events:
  - patient_registered
  - patient_demographics_corrected
  - patient_uhid_corrected (admin only)
  - registration_duplicate_override
  - duplicate_resolved
- phi_access (log_phi_read):
  - patient_index_searched, with the matched ids
  - registration_record_viewed, registration_match_viewed
  - opd_consultation_viewed, op_patients_listed
- clinical_record:
  - opd_visit_called/skipped/recalled/assigned
  - opd_consultation_saved/signed/addendum (signed is written in-transaction)
  - opd_visit_completed with disposition
  - appointment_rescheduled/checked_in/no_show
- clinical_access, in-transaction: opd_converted_to_admission, patient_readmitted.
- configuration: clinic session and charge rule changes.
- target_id is always a string, which avoids the known int-hash chain break.
- The socket carries no PHI: 'opd:queue_changed' sends the department only, and clients refetch through scoped, audited REST. The board carries no PHI and is not audited.

8. LINKS TO OTHER EPICS
- adt:
  - Conversion uses the adt-1 bed picker when it lands (free-text ward and bed plus admission_choices until then).
  - One patients-status rebuild should carry adt's and death-record statuses too.

- medorder: an OPD Rx is an outpatient-setting order in the single store, screened by medication_safety_gate.enforce_medication_safety(entry_point='opd_prescription'). It never writes medications rows (the eMAR reads those) or helix orders directly.
- grn / pharmacy: OP dispensing consumes the medorder store; no dependency from here.
- lis: OPD investigations are orders tagged with opd_visit_id; results come through lis-1; health check packages come later.
- site (multi-site): the UHID series is group-wide; site_id on opd_visits, clinic_sessions and appointments arrives with site-1.
- ABDM: the placeholder only; M1 creation comes later.
- workforce: leave becomes a session exception (later).
- Ward Record: shares the identity core (role batch, hospital-number mode, admit-existing).

product_rulings.question: OPD-S1 (new, patient safety): before the desk attaches a visit, or a clinician attaches an admission, to an EXISTING patient record found by search, which identifiers must be confirmed?
product_rulings.options: (a) two identifiers shown and confirmed with the patient (name plus DOB or stated age, plus UHID), recorded in the audit; (b) UHID alone; (c) a name match alone
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Wrong-patient selection attaches someone else's allergies and history. This also governs the Ward Record clerk's returning-patient screen.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S2 (new, patient safety): when registration finds a probable duplicate, should the server warn or block?
product_rulings.options: (a) warn, require a reason, audit it and open a worklist item; hard refusal only on exact UHID or active ABHA; (b) block above the threshold until a supervisor reviews; (c) warn only, no reason
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Duplicate charts split the allergy history, but blocking a sick walk-in at the counter is worse. Default ORB_DUPLICATE_MODE=warn.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S3 (new, patient safety, the analogue of held W111; this does not decide W111): do vitals taken in OPD enter the observation chart and count as the patient's latest vitals after OPD-to-IP conversion?
product_rulings.options: (a) no: they stay inside the OPD record, are shown on the admission form with their time, and the ward charts a fresh set; (b) copy them into vitals at conversion
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Otherwise hours-old OPD values become the board's latest reading and its NEWS2.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S4 (new, patient safety, related to held R010): do active OPD prescriptions carry onto the inpatient medication chart at conversion?
product_rulings.options: (a) never automatically: they are listed as OPD or home medicines for item-by-item reconciliation by the admitting prescriber; (b) carry them as active inpatient orders
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The eMAR would otherwise offer a nurse a take-home prescription as an inpatient dose.

product_rulings.question: OPD-S5 (new, patient safety): may the front desk record allergies or 'no known allergies' at registration?
product_rulings.options: (a) no allergy field at the desk; a clinician captures allergies at consultation or admission; (b) the desk may record allergies but never NKDA; (c) the desk records both
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), which is how opd-4 is built. A clerk-typed NKDA would silence the interlock.

product_rulings.question: N1: where does the UHID come from at each site, and in what format?
product_rulings.options: hospital mode (type the existing HIS number, site regex); orb mode (Orb series with a Verhoeff check digit, site prefix)
product_rulings.recommendation: Hospital mode by default (beside-HIS, Ward Record); orb mode with a check digit for a site Orb replaces. Never reset per year.

product_rulings.question: N2: how long does an OPD visit let that clinic's staff read the patient's chart?
product_rulings.options: same day only; 7 days; 30 days; until the follow-up appointment
product_rulings.recommendation: 7 days (ORB_OPD_SCOPE_DAYS), and only while the patient has no active admission elsewhere.

product_rulings.question: N3: create a receptionist role, and should it also take consent (F123) and money?
product_rulings.options: new role with registration only; plus consent.record; plus payments.record
product_rulings.recommendation: New role holding registration.read and registration.write plus consent.record once counsel agrees. Money stays with the cashier role, so one person at a combined desk uses two accounts.

product_rulings.question: N4: may a ward-scoped doctor search the whole patient index (name, UHID, age, sex only) to avoid duplicate registrations?
product_rulings.options: yes, minimal fields, audited; no, own department only
product_rulings.recommendation: Yes, minimal fields, minimum 3 characters, 20 results, every search audited with the matched ids.

product_rulings.question: N5 (existing R018): must the desk capture date of birth?
product_rulings.options: required; optional with stated age
product_rulings.recommendation: Optional, with stated age stored with its date and the 'no date of birth, no discharge link' hint. Never store an estimated DOB.

product_rulings.question: N6: when is the consultation fee charged, and is there a registration fee or free follow-up window?
product_rulings.options: at registration (prepaid) or at completion (today); REG-FEE yes or no; follow-up window in days
product_rulings.recommendation: Site setting, default completion. A follow-up window maps to its own OPD-FOLLOWUP code the site prices, never an implicit zero.

product_rulings.question: N7: what does the waiting-room token board show?
product_rulings.options: token only; token and initials; token and name
product_rulings.recommendation: Token, doctor and room only (DPDP).

product_rulings.question: N8: when Orb runs the OPD, may a visit be completed without a signed consultation note?
product_rulings.options: signed note required; allowed with a reason ('note on paper')
product_rulings.recommendation: Allowed with a reason, because many clinics will keep paper notes at first.

product_rulings.question: N9: which queue priority categories apply?
product_rulings.options: none; senior citizen, pregnant, differently abled, emergency; site list
product_rulings.recommendation: A site-configured list with a reason captured, shown on the doctor's queue.

product_rulings.question: N10: what identity document data may registration store?
product_rulings.options: none; type plus last 4; full number
product_rulings.recommendation: Type plus last 4, and never a full Aadhaar number (Aadhaar Act); counsel to confirm.

risks: The patients rebuild (opd-2) is an FK-parent rebuild under 35 child tables, done in an autocommit window that commits the runner's earlier work. A defect here loses or orphans patient rows. Mitigations: the proven _atomic_table_rebuild path, a frozen column list, row-count and foreign_key_check assertions, a verified backup before upgrade, and a dry run on a copy of the dev DB (isolated verify stack). It runs on every install, Ward Record included, even with the flags off.

Every new role is a users rebuild (FK parent of about 20 tables). The canonical column list in _rebuild_users_role_check is hard-coded, so any epic that ADDs a users column (for example qualification for prescriptions) must update it in the same change or the next role migration aborts. Batch receptionist, the Ward Record clerk and other epics' roles into one migration.

Migration version collisions: about ten sessions plus several epic architects will all claim numbers after 47. Two agents picking the same version gives a duplicate schema_migrations key and a server that will not boot (migrations.py m20 docstring). Reserve number blocks per epic before building.

The OPD scope arm widens who can read a chart. A wrong window, or forgetting the no-active-admission rule, re-opens the 2026-08-05 class of cross-ward reads, or lets a front-desk visit launder access to another ward's inpatient. It ships flag-gated, with every guarded route re-run against an OPD fixture.
Wrong-patient selection at the returning-patient search, and split duplicate charts, both lose allergy history. Those are the main clinical hazards of this epic (OPD-S1, OPD-S2, OPD-S5).

Audit volume: queue screens polled every few seconds would write one encrypted phi_access row per poll, and audit already drives storage at 200 beds. Content-free socket nudges with refetch-on-change keep reads proportional to changes.

Search performance: name LIKE scans over 100k+ patients in SQLCipher may be slow. opd-4 and opd-5 must measure at 100k rows and fall back to prefix keys. FTS5 availability in sqlcipher3-wheels is unverified.

OPD prescription depends on medorder-1. The tempting shortcut of writing OPD prescriptions into the medications table would put take-home drugs on the eMAR. A test must forbid it, and no fourth store may be built.

The lazy front-desk schema trap: a migration that ALTERs opd_visits before ensure_frontdesk_schema has created it would be ledgered as done with the columns missing. opd-1 folds the tables into the ledger first.

Lane competition: this epic is about 62 engineer-days, about 72 with browser re-verification and merge friction, which is about 4 calendar months at the sales plan's 4 engineer-days a week. It competes directly with the Ward Record build (28 to 44.5 days), which is the only paid product. The minimum useful slice (walk-in to billed consultation, no appointments, no Rx: opd-1 to opd-8, opd-10, opd-11, opd-13, opd-14) is about 40 days.

Device class: the OPD screens must never show NEWS2, a band or AI advice (R023, the Ward Record no-score rule). OPD vitals stay in the OPD record and the existing AST scoring guard covers opd_service.

DPDP minimisation: new demographic fields (email, alternate phone, guardian) widen the record. They are classified under clinical_record retention, and the consent_service text saying Orb holds no separate contact store must stay true.

Prescription print needs the doctor's qualification, which Orb does not store (credentialing gap). Until the workforce or credentialing epic adds it, the print carries only the name and users.registration_number.
